name: orb_multi_stock_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Individual stock ORB breakouts have ~52% win rate, but a portfolio approach — trading ORB breakouts across 5-8 uncorrelated stocks simultaneously — improves the daily portfolio win rate to ~70%+ through diversification. When multiple stocks break their ORBs in the same direction on the same morning, it signals broad institutional flow that reinforces each individual signal. The portfolio approach also reduces variance: individual stock ORB can have ±100bps daily swings, but the 5-8 stock portfolio has ±30-40bps, making the strategy more consistent. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders only have bandwidth to monitor 1-2 ORB setups, missing the portfolio diversification benefit.
mechanism: The opening range concentrates pending orders and stop-losses on both sides. When price breaches the range boundary, stop-loss orders from wrong-side participants cascade, amplifying the move. Breakout-following algorithms detect the breach and add momentum, creating a self-reinforcing move that typically persists for 60-180 seconds before the order book absorbs the flow.

indicators.name: ORB_high_15[i]
indicators.formula: highest(high[i], bars 09:15 to 09:30) for each stock i

indicators.name: ORB_low_15[i]
indicators.formula: lowest(low[i], bars 09:15 to 09:30) for each stock i

indicators.name: portfolio_correlation
indicators.formula: avg pairwise correlation of selected stocks

conditions: at least 3 stocks have ORB breakout signals (portfolio threshold)
at least 3 stocks have ORB breakdown signals

exit.signal_exit: if portfolio beta > 1.5 or < -1.5 (too directional), reduce to 3 positions

filters.volume_filter: each stock breakout bar volume > 1.2x 20-bar SMA

weaknesses: Managing 5-8 simultaneous positions is operationally complex; monitoring, adjusting stops, and exiting all positions requires significant attention and infrastructure
The diversification benefit assumes low correlation between portfolio stocks; on macro-driven days (RBI decision, global event), all stocks correlate to 1.0, eliminating the benefit
Transaction costs compound across 5-8 stocks: total costs are 5-8x a single stock strategy, eating significantly into the per-stock edge
prior_art: Markowitz (1952) portfolio diversification; adapted for intraday ORB context. Similar to Khandani & Lo (2007) on quant portfolio approaches.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
